ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All disclosed beneficial owners, directors, senior officers, and authorized representatives must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list, the Taiwan Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) rogue list, and the PRC Ministry of Public Security list. PEPs are identified through a FATF-aligned risk-based algorithm, including close associates and family members, subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Sanctions screening must be repeated at least daily via a commercial compliance tool, and all hits must be escalated to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer and approved for file. Negative news and adverse media screening must cover the preceding 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commercial Registration One-Stop System - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Query Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Taiwan's Company Act, the company name must contain a unique appellation, a trade name, a business scope qualifier, and the legal form suffix. The legal name must be written in traditional Chinese characters. English letters, Arabic numerals, and Mandarin phonetic transliterations are permitted only as supplementary elements and must not be used as the sole name. Phonetic transliteration into Mandarin must comply with ROC Ministry of Education Pinyin or Zhuyin standards. For a Sino-foreign equity joint venture, the foreign investor's own name may be transliterated into Chinese and used as part of the appellation subject to no conflict with prior registrants.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon the issuance of an official name rejection from MOEA, the applicant must within 30 days file a written reconsideration application with the MOEA Central Company Registration Bureau, stating the grounds and attaching a revised name or supplementary evidence. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may, within 30 days after service of the denial, initiate an administrative appeal before the Executive Yuan. The Executive Yuan determination may then be contested through administrative litigation in the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months. All submissions must reference the original name pre-query tracking number and include a certified traditional Chinese translation of any foreign-origin name components.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Temporary virtual office addresses provided by registered agents are accepted only for provisional incorporation; however, the Ministry of Finance and local tax bureaus reject mail-forwarding-only addresses for unified business tax registration. Banks similarly deny high-risk KYB for virtual office addresses. For an AI data-labeling BPO, the entity must maintain a physical operating center in Taiwan, with leased premises, employer payroll, employee presence, computing hardware, and visible signage. Failure to prove commercial substance will be treated as fictitious incorporation under Company Act Article 10, leading to deregistration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: MOEA and municipal business registration authorities, in coordination with the National Taxation Bureau, may perform unannounced physical inspections of registered offices. Newly incorporated BPO entities face an annual inspection probability of approximately 0.5 to 2.5 percent based on national statistics; however, the probability rises to 12.5 percent if the registered address is a virtual office or shared mailbox, and to 15 percent if the office is a pure virtual agent without any usufruct. The inspection checklist covers lease execution, office equipment, active employee posts, attendance and payroll records, fire safety and occupational hazard compliance, business books, and standardized VAT invoice issuance terminals.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (Company Act, Republic of China) - Articles 1-2 (types of companies), 128-130 (incorporators and share subscription), 156 (share capital flexibility), 161-162 (share certificates), 193-203 (board of directors operations), 208-210 (chairperson and legal representative), 266-273 (capital increase and foreign investment alignment); together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals Articles 1-20 and the Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Central Commercial Registry; online via the MOEA Company Registration Information System (CRIS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application for Incorporation, submitted together with the Certified Articles of Incorporation and required supporting forms through the MOEA Company Registration Information System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for a general company limited by shares in Taiwan; the Company Act abolished the minimum paid-in capital requirement. For a foreign-invested company, the MOEA Investment Commission verifies that stated capital is commensurate with the approved business plan and projected operational scale. No blocked escrow account is mandated. Paid-in capital may be remitted from overseas as foreign currency, converted in a Taiwan bank, evidenced by an inward remittance certificate, and verified by a Taiwan certified public accountant.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION

WHEREAS, the Company, Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Ltd., is organized as a company limited by shares under the Republic of China (Taiwan) Company Act, and the incorporators have subscribed to the entire initial share capital;

WHEREAS, the business scope has been approved by the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs as a digital business process outsourcing enterprise providing computer vision bounding-box annotation and RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback) data curation services under ISIC 8220;

WHEREAS, the incorporators have convened this organizational meeting to adopt the initial resolutions and to constitute the First Board of Directors;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. The Articles of Incorporation presented to this meeting are approved and adopted as the governing constitution of the Company, effective upon registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

2. The authorized share capital is fixed at New Taiwan Dollars TEN MILLION, divided into 1,000,000 ordinary shares of New Taiwan Dollars TEN par value each. All issued shares have been fully subscribed by the initial shareholder, and the full paid-up capital has been deposited in the Company capital bank account.

3. The registered office of the Company is fixed at 10F, No. 88, Minzu East Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei City 104, Taiwan (R.O.C.). The Board ratifies the lease and use-right documents and authorizes the Chairperson to execute any amendments or extensions thereof.

4. The following persons are elected and appointed as statutory officers: [Name] as Director and Chairperson; [Name] as Director and General Manager; [Name] as Corporate Secretary and Compliance Officer; and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer. Each officer has consented to serve in such capacity and is authorized to act within the respective scope of duties.

5. The banking institution of the Company is designated as [Bank Name, Branch]. The Chairperson, General Manager, and Chief Financial Officer are appointed as authorized joint signatories. Any two of the appointed authorized officers shall jointly sign all banking instructions, wire transfers, payment orders, and payment-platform instructions, including the Mass PayPal Payout and Wise remittance rails identified as target payment channels.

6. The Directors and officers are expressly instructed to (i) file the incorporation application with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; (ii) obtain the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Certificate and tax identification number from the National Taxation Bureau; (iii) register employees with the labor and health insurance authorities; (iv) adopt accounting books and an anti-money-laundering compliance manual appropriate to a low-risk digital BPO entity; and (v) execute all ancillary filings, declarations, and undertakings necessary to bring the Company into full legal operation.

7. The Chairperson or General Manager may delegate to legal counsel the completion of governmental filings and may affix the Company seal in order to perfect any authorizations required under the Company Act or administrative regulations.

This resolution is effective immediately upon unanimous approval by the incorporators and directors, and it shall be filed with the minutes of the organizational meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Company Registration Information System (CRIS) Online Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an automated company name pre-approval application through the MOEA CRIS portal by entering two to four Chinese corporate name alternatives and one English company name. The system screens against existing registered Taiwanese companies and reserved marks. Once the proposed name clears conflict checks, print the provisional approval certificate. If the chosen name contains Taiwan or any word implying state sponsorship, attach a letter of intent from the foreign investor and the proposed board clearly explaining the lawful use. Retain the name approval letter because it must be filed with the incorporation application within six months of issuance.
required_dossiers: Completed Company Name Pre-Approval Application Form
Proposed Corporate Names in Chinese and English
Copy of Foreign Investor Identity Document or Incorporation Certificate
Power of Attorney if Filing Through a Local Agent
Non-Conflict Statement or Trademark Search Report
Shareholder Identity List
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the system rejects or queries the name because of similarity to an existing company or prohibited terminology, the applicant may file a formal amendment within 14 days by substituting a new name. A final administrative denial is subject to an administrative petition to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days; in most cases expedience is achieved by resubmitting a distinct name with a differentiating prefix or geographic qualifier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval by the Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the Foreign Investment Application Form for a corporate investor, together with the draft Articles of Incorporation, an investment plan, source-of-funds evidence, and a description of the AI data labeling operations. The Investment Commission screens the project against the reserved or restricted certificate list. Upon approval, it issues the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, which is a mandatory precondition to the final incorporation registration. The foreign shareholder must remit the approved capital amount from an overseas account into Taiwan through the banking system and retain the exchange settlement and inward remittance receipts for later CPA verification.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Certified Copy of the Foreign Investor s Certificate of Incorporation or Passport
Bank Reference and Source of Funds Statement
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Investment and Business Plan for AI Data Labeling BPO
Power of Attorney for the Local Agent
Resume and Criminal Record Declaration of Proposed Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission suspends the application for clarification, the applicant must submit a supplementary opinion, corrected business plan, or revised investment amount within 30 days. If the Commission issues a formal rejection, the applicant may file an administrative petition with the Executive Yuan within 30 days, or cure the stated defect and resubmit the application with a fresh cover letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance, Organizational Meeting, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Taiwan Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and the First Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause the foreign shareholder to transfer the fully subscribed capital into a newly opened temporary capital account at a licensed Taiwan bank. Obtain from the bank a certificate of paid-in capital deposit and the foreign exchange settlement receipt. Concurrently, convene an organizational meeting of the incorporators and first board of directors to approve the Articles of Incorporation and the pro-forma first board resolution. The independent CPA must examine the bank certificate, verify the identity of the subscriber, confirm the exchange rate and lawful conversion, trace the inward remittance, and issue a formal capital verification report. The report must state that the share capital has been fully paid in cash and that no asset inflation or back-to-back loan exists.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the Incorporators Organizational Meeting
Pro-Forma First Board Resolution
Bank Certificate of Paid-In Capital
Foreign Exchange Settlement Receipt and Inward Remittance Certificate
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Shareholders Register and Directors Consent Letters
CPA Capital Verification Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CPA identifies a funding shortfall or mismatch in the remitting entity, the foreign investor must top up the difference within 10 business days and obtain a corrected bank certificate. If the bank refuses to issue the capital certificate due to clerical errors, provide an amended remittance instruction and resubmit the report. A materially defective verification report may be redone by a second CPA without penalty if submitted before final registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Registration Filing with MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application through the CRIS portal or at the designated MOEA service window, whichever is permitted for the registered office jurisdiction. Attach the company name reservation certificate, the final certified Articles of Incorporation, the minutes of the organizational meeting, the first board resolution, the CPA capital verification report, the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, the registered office lease or consent letter, and all director and shareholder identity documents. Pay the statutory registration fee online or at the counter and obtain an official receipt. The registry will examine legal compliance, capital verification, corporate name sufficiency, governance structure, and the business scope description. Upon approval, the registry issue the Company Incorporation Certificate and automatically coordinate with the National Taxation Bureau for the tax identification number.
required_dossiers: Company Name Pre-Approval Certificate
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of Incorporation Meeting and First Board Resolution
CPA Capital Verification Report
Foreign Investment Approval Letter from the Investment Commission
Registered Office Address Consent, Lease, or Title Evidence
Photocopies of Directors and Shareholders Identity Documents
Company Registration Fee Payment Receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or a supplemental notice, the applicant must rectify within 30 days, supplying the missing document or a written explanation. If an incorporation application is formally rejected, the applicant may cure the defect and resubmit as a new application or file an administrative appeal within 30 days of receipt of the rejection notice. The registry may also, upon request, issue a provisional certificate pending final approval where only immaterial omissions remain.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration and Ancillary Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (local branch), Labor and Health Insurance Administration Office, and Local Fire Safety Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Incorporation Certificate, register the entity with the local National Taxation Bureau as a profit-seeking enterprise and obtain the certificate of registration for tax identification and the taxable statement for value-added business tax. The tax office may require submission of the bank account certification, lease agreement, and a Business Conditions Questionnaire. Then enroll the company as a new employer with the labor and health insurance authorities; the AI data labeling operation must maintain employee records and payroll ledgers. Because the business is a pure digital BPO and not a manufacturing facility, only standard office fire safety clearance, inspection of electrical wiring, and workspace safety compliance are required; no industrial operating license triggers.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Certificate
Registered Office Lease Agreement
Tax Registration Application and Profit-Seeking Enterprise Filing
Business Conditions Questionnaire
Bank Account Certification and Corporate Seal Registration
Employer Registration Forms for Labor and Health Insurance
Official Rent Receipt or Utility Bill
Fire Safety Inspection Certificate for Office Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority delays or issues a correction notice because the described business does not align with the tax code, submit a revised business description with reference to ISIC 8220 and NAICS 518210. Unpaid tax registration fines are avoidable by making a voluntary supplemental filing within 15 days of the relevant notice. Insurance registration errors are corrected by resubmitting the employee roster and payroll ledger with a written statement verifying the effective registration date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the subject company performs computer vision bounding-box annotation and RLHF data curation operations classified as a pure digital BPO service. No manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility is part of the approved scope (ISIC 8220).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial or manufacturing operating license is required. The company holds only the standard Company Incorporation Certificate from the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Registration from the National Taxation Bureau.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration (EPA) has no regulatory trigger for office-based AI data labeling activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the operation is not listed in the quantifiable categories requiring a full Environmental Impact Assessment report or an environmental registration; no construction, physical processing, chemical usage, or hazardous waste generation is involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, particulate emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated. General office waste must be disposed of under the Taiwan Waste Management Act, and computer equipment shall be recycled through EPA-registered electronic waste recyclers in accordance with the Resource Recycling and Circular Economy Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as to manufacturing. For the leased office floor, the local fire department requires a standard fire safety inspection certificate under the Fire Services Act; the building must have valid structural load approval and fire evacuation facilities. Workplace safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act applies only to ergonomic workstations, electrical outlets, and emergency lighting. These are routine occupancy certifications, not industrial licenses.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (財政部賦稅署) and the local National Taxation Bureau (國稅局) via the online portal 'Taxation and Customs Administration e-Services' (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested entity such as a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, the company must first complete company incorporation with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) to obtain a Company Registration Number. Subsequently, within 15 days of incorporation, the company must file a 'Business Registration Application' (營業登記申請) with the local National Taxation Bureau, submitting the incorporation certificate, lease or ownership proof of the business premises, identification of the responsible person, and the company seal. The Bureau will issue a 'Unified Business Number' (統一編號) which serves as the Tax Identification Number (TIN) for both income tax and business tax (VAT) purposes. For foreign non-resident entities without a fixed place of business, a tax representative must be appointed and a 'Tax Registration for Foreign Enterprises' (外國公司稅籍登記) filed with the same bureau, using the representative's address as the service address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Taiwan does not offer check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; the entity is taxed as a separate taxable entity under the Income Tax Act and Business Tax Act)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory for all businesses with a fixed place of business in Taiwan; no turnover threshold applies. For cross-border electronic services provided by foreign entities, a threshold of NT$ 300,000 per year applies before mandatory registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the use of Uniform Invoices (統一發票) for all VAT-registered businesses. Since 2021, the government has promoted the Electronic Uniform Invoice (電子統一發票) system, requiring businesses to transmit invoice data in real-time to the Ministry of Finance's 'Invoice Cloud' (發票存摺) platform via the 'Turnkey' (加值中心) API. For B2B transactions, the 'E-Invoice Turnkey' system must be used for electronic exchange. The system includes anti-fraud digital stamping through the 'Invoice Encryption' mechanism, and businesses must issue invoices within 48 hours of transaction completion.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, zero-rating applies to (a) exported goods, (b) services provided to foreign clients and used entirely outside Taiwan, (c) services related to international transport, and (d) goods sold to duty-free shops. For AI data labeling and BPO services, the service must be performed in Taiwan but delivered to a foreign client, with the contract clearly stating the foreign recipient and the service being used abroad. The provider must retain evidence of the foreign client's identity and the offshore use of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) - for physical goods
Bill of Lading (提單) or Airway Bill (空運提單) - for physical goods
Inward Remittance Certificate (匯入匯款通知書) or Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (外匯結售證明) - for services and goods
Service Contract (服務合約) - for services, detailing the foreign recipient and scope
Invoice (發票) - the zero-rated invoice issued to the foreign client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, if a zero-rated claim is found to be fraudulent or unsubstantiated, the tax authority will assess the VAT at 5% retroactively, impose a penalty of up to 5 times the underpaid tax, and may impose a criminal fine of up to NT$ 1,000,000 for willful evasion. Additionally, the taxpayer must pay interest on the underpaid tax from the original due date. The National Taxation Bureau conducts post-clearance audits on export documentation, and any discrepancy in the FX repatriation deadline or missing documentation will trigger a clawback of the zero-rating benefit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), with foreign-exchange reporting and banking supervision supplemented by the Financial Supervisory Commission, the Ministry of Finance Customs Administration, and, for investment involving Mainland China persons or capital, the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Two Sides of the Taiwan Strait.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is generally convertible for bona fide current-account transactions, including trade, services, payroll, dividends, interest, and approved operating expenses. Taiwan does not generally impose a blanket surrender requirement on export proceeds. Banks must verify the transaction purpose, supporting documents, remitter and beneficiary identity, and applicable reporting thresholds. Capital-account transactions, securities investments, acquisitions, foreign direct investment, Mainland China-related investments, and certain lending or guarantees may require prior approval, registration, or documentary reporting. A Taiwan company may generally remit dividends or other distributions after audited financial statements, shareholder or board approvals, tax clearance, withholding-tax compliance, and satisfaction of capital-maintenance and corporate-law requirements. A remittance involving Mainland China ownership or a Mainland China-origin source of funds requires separate eligibility, ownership, investment-approval, and foreign-exchange analysis. Profits cannot be remitted merely because cash is available if accounting profits, distributable reserves, tax filings, or required approvals are incomplete.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan has no general statutory rule requiring exporters or service providers to convert a fixed percentage of export or service receipts into New Taiwan dollars within a prescribed period. Foreign-currency receipts may generally be retained in permitted foreign-currency accounts, subject to bank reporting, transaction-purpose verification, anti-money-laundering controls, and applicable declaration thresholds. For goods exports, customs declarations and export documentation support the underlying transaction. For cross-border data-labeling and AI-training services, invoices, contracts, delivery evidence, customer acceptance records, and service descriptions should substantiate the service receipt. A Taiwan bank may require a foreign-exchange declaration or supporting documents for transactions exceeding applicable regulatory thresholds or presenting unusual risk. If proceeds are received through PayPal, Wise, or another offshore payment institution, the company should transfer funds to its Taiwan corporate account through a licensed bank, reconcile gross receipts and fees, and retain platform statements and settlement reports. Mainland China-origin export or service receipts may be subject to Mainland China SAFE, banking, tax, and customs rules before funds can be remitted to Taiwan.

Taipei Fubon Commercial Bank Co., Ltd.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for collections and payout support, but low as a replacement for a Taiwan licensed-bank relationship. Wise is a payment service provider rather than a Taiwan deposit-taking bank and should not be treated as the company's statutory operating, escrow, or capital account. PayPal Payouts and similar mass-payout products are product-, country-, merchant-, and underwriting-dependent; availability, settlement currency, recipient eligibility, reserve rights, transaction limits, and chargeback controls must be confirmed in writing. Offshore digital EMIs may impose enhanced verification, suspend balances, restrict Mainland China-related activity, or reject data-services transactions involving personal data, artificial-intelligence training, sanctioned parties, or high-volume individual payees. Use licensed Taiwan banks for capital injections, tax payments, payroll, dividends, treasury concentration, and final settlement. Use fintech channels only under a documented payment-flow policy with platform terms, transaction-level reconciliation, beneficiary screening, and contingency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Taiwan banks may permit remote preliminary onboarding, but final account opening is discretionary and commonly requires authenticated corporate records, beneficial-owner verification, specimen signatures, certified identification, and a video or in-person interview. Physical attendance by every director is not universally mandatory; the bank may require attendance by authorized representatives, directors, controlling shareholders, or ultimate beneficial owners, particularly where the shareholder chain includes Mainland China persons, offshore entities, nominee arrangements, unusual business models, or high transaction volumes. Documents issued outside Taiwan may require notarization, legalization, apostille treatment where accepted, Chinese translation, and current corporate-register evidence. The company should maintain a Taiwan-resident authorized contact and a board resolution granting clear account and payment authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ownership, inconsistent use of China and Taiwan entity identifiers, or an ownership chain involving Mainland China individuals, state-linked entities, nominee shareholders, or unregistered beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles and corporate registry extracts; complete ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and addresses; shareholder register; joint-venture contract; capital-contribution evidence; director and officer register; related-party disclosure; Taiwan investment approvals or filings; Mainland China approvals or registrations where applicable; board resolutions; and a written explanation reconciling all legal names, registration numbers, jurisdictions, and tax identifiers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from Mainland China, an offshore holding company, or a third party rather than directly from the registered investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-contribution agreement; approved investment documents; bank-origin evidence; remitter-to-investor relationship proof; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth memorandum; audited financial statements; tax returns; board approval; investment-purpose declaration; beneficial-owner confirmation; and bank pre-clearance of the remittance route. Do not use unrelated third-party remitters without documented legal and commercial justification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description appears generic, but actual activity involves AI model training, personal data, biometric data, sensitive datasets, content moderation, or cross-border data transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service catalogue; customer contracts and statements of work; data-processing addenda; data classification matrix; consent or lawful-basis analysis; Taiwan Personal Data Protection Act compliance memorandum; information-security policies; access-control and encryption standards; data-residency and transfer map; subcontractor register; prohibited-content policy; customer and dataset provenance controls; export-control screening; and evidence that the company does not provide regulated AI, surveillance, or restricted technology services without required approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume mass payouts to individuals, freelancers, or beneficiaries located in multiple countries, especially where payments are round-dollar, repetitive, or routed through payment platforms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficiary master-file controls; signed contractor agreements; invoices or task records; identity and tax-residency information; sanctions and adverse-media screening; payment-purpose taxonomy; payroll or contractor classification analysis; approval matrix; segregation of duties; transaction-monitoring rules; exception reports; platform settlement statements; and monthly reconciliation from customer receipt to beneficiary payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of PayPal, Wise, virtual accounts, or offshore wallets inconsistent with the bank's expected-account profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy; platform terms and account ownership evidence; bank statements; customer invoices; settlement reports; fee schedules; chargeback and reserve policy; flow-of-funds diagram; expected monthly volume and currencies; counterparties by country; contingency funding plan; and confirmation that the receiving account is held in the legal entity's name rather than an employee, agent, or unrelated affiliate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, cyber-risk, or prohibited-country exposure involving customers, workers, data subjects, software, or payment beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer and beneficiary screening logs; sanctions-policy document; restricted-party screening results; country-risk matrix; contract representations; end-use and end-user certifications; software and technology classification; escalation records; blocked-party procedures; periodic rescreening evidence; and legal review for United Nations, Taiwan, United States, European Union, and applicable Mainland China restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained related-party transfers, circular payments, shareholder loans, intercompany netting, or rapid movement of capital through newly opened accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; invoices; loan agreements; repayment schedules; board approvals; accounting ledgers; tax treatment; beneficial-owner analysis; economic-purpose memorandum; cash-flow forecast; and evidence of arm's-length pricing and actual delivery of services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared low-risk BPO activity and unusually large foreign-exchange turnover or cash-intensive activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year operating budget; customer pipeline; signed contracts; historical bank statements; staffing plan; payroll forecast; unit economics; expected currency exposure; customer concentration analysis; invoice-aging report; management accounts; and a transaction-volume bridge explaining receipts, platform fees, contractor payouts, taxes, and retained liquidity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Open a Taiwan corporate capital or designated investment account before remittance. Obtain all required company-registration, foreign-investment, and Mainland China-related approvals or filings before funds are sent. The registered investor should remit directly from an account in its own name through a regulated bank using SWIFT, ordinarily with MT103 payment instructions and accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, purpose, currency, and invoice or capital-contribution references. The receiving bank should pre-review the remittance purpose, investor identity, beneficial ownership, source of funds, capital amount, and permitted use. Do not split transfers to avoid review, use personal accounts, route funds through unrelated affiliates, or describe capital as trade receipts. For a Taiwan company, retain the bank advice, inward-remittance confirmation, foreign-exchange declaration, capital-contribution evidence, accounting entry, and corporate-registration or investment-filing evidence. If the funds originate in Mainland China, complete applicable SAFE foreign-exchange registration, outbound-investment or cross-border payment procedures, tax documentation, and Taiwan-side investment approvals before attempting settlement. Convert only the amount required for operating liquidity; retain permitted balances in USD, EUR, or other supported currencies where commercially appropriate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for ordinary vendor, contractor, tax, and service payments after invoice, contract, beneficiary, sanctions, and tax review. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, including confirmed or unconfirmed import LCs, only where the counterparty, goods, documentary conditions, and bank risk justify the cost. For service procurement and AI-data operations, maintain executed agreements, purchase orders, invoices, acceptance evidence, timesheets or task logs, withholding-tax analysis, beneficiary bank details, and proof of sanctions screening. Establish payment cut-off times, dual authorization, callback verification for changed bank details, segregation of preparation and release, and daily payment-limit monitoring. For platform settlements, distinguish customer collections, platform fees, refunds, reserves, and net payouts in the ledger. Use domestic Taiwan clearing for local New Taiwan dollar payments and bank-based international rails for foreign currency; do not rely on informal value transfer, cryptocurrency settlement, or personal-wallet pass-throughs. Reconcile each outbound payment to a contract, invoice, approved beneficiary, accounting code, and applicable tax or foreign-exchange reporting record.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a Taiwan authorized bank for forecast or committed USD, EUR, JPY, or other supported receivables and payables, subject to bank suitability, credit limits, documentation, and evidence of an underlying exposure.

Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management and currency-tenor matching, subject to bank approval, approved dealing limits, collateral or margin terms, and accurate recording of the spot and forward legs.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies where physical delivery is restricted or unavailable, only where offered by an authorized counterparty and permitted under applicable Taiwan and counterparty-jurisdiction rules. Document the hedged exposure, fixing source, settlement currency, valuation, and close-out terms.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for material, recurring currency exposures, subject to board-approved treasury limits, counterparty credit assessment, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, accounting treatment, and legal review.

Plain-vanilla FX options or collars may be considered for material exposures where the bank confirms legal availability and the company understands premium, settlement, valuation, and potential-obligation risks. Avoid leveraged, path-dependent, or speculative products unless separately approved by the board and supported by a documented risk-management policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Directors, Supervisors, Managers and Major Shareholders (Company Act Article 22-1) — Annual UBO and register confirmation for anti-money-laundering compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Competent Authority — Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) via the Company Directors and Major Shareholders Information Declaration Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 each calendar year (information as of December 31 of the prior year); any change affecting the declared 10%-or-more shareholders or officers must be re-declared within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to NT$500,000 (≈USD 16,000) with a rectification order; per-occurrence fines for continued default; willful non-filing may be treated as an AML-control deficiency affecting banking relationships

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and Undistributed Surplus (Retained Earnings) Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Regional Branches), Ministry of Finance, ROC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 – May 31 for calendar-year taxpayers (within the 5th month after the fiscal year end; approved non-calendar years follow the equivalent 5th-month rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 3% late-filing surcharge (滯報金) on assessed tax after a 15-day rectification notice; 9% willful non-filing fine (怠報金) for continued default; unpaid tax accrues a 1% delinquency penalty for every 2 days up to 30 days, then referral to the Administrative Enforcement Agency; estimated assessment by tax authority

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) of Shareholders — adoption of Business Report, Audited/Reviewed Financial Statements and Profit-Distribution Proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' Meeting (corporate act); resolutions later recordable with MOEA (director change registrations within 15 days)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened on or before June 30 (within 6 months after the December 31 fiscal year end); MOEA registration of newly elected directors/supervisors within 15 days after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible persons subject to fines (typically NT$10,000–NT$50,000 per violation) for failure to convene; MOEA may convene the meeting on shareholder petition or order dissolution if the company has ceased business for more than 6 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Business Report, Financial Statements and Earnings-Distribution/Deficit-Offsetting Proposal with the Company Registry (Company Act Article 20)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs — Central/Regional Company Registration Office (商業司/中部辦公室)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after adoption at the AGM (by July 30 for calendar-year companies holding the latest lawful AGM on June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Per-occurrence fines of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 imposed on the responsible person for non-filing after notice; repeated non-compliance can trigger MOEA dissolution proceedings under Company Act Article 10

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Operational Status Survey / Report for Overseas Chinese and Foreign-Invested Enterprises (僑外投資事業營運狀況調查)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: As announced each year by MOEAIC, typically due within the first quarter (by March 31) covering the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond may prejudice pending or future investment-permit and foreign-exchange remittance applications under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; MOEAIC may initiate administrative inquiry and mandate correction

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit for non-public companies when paid-in capital ≥ NT$30,000,000 (≈USD 1,000,000), or annual net operating revenue ≥ NT$30,000,000, or accumulated deficit ≥ one-third of paid-in capital, or when MOEA otherwise directs; financial institutions, public companies and companies designated by the FSC are audited regardless of size. The assessed entity (AI data-labeling BPO) must determine the audit requirement annually against these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Business Entity Accounting Act (商業會計法), Enterprise Accounting Standards Gazette (企業會計準則公報, EAS — IFRS-aligned for non-public companies); public companies apply FSC-endorsed IFRS; statutory books and financial statements must be prepared in New Taiwan Dollars with calendar-year accounting unless a different fiscal year is approved

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the JV must annually confirm and declare to the MOEA online platform, by March 31, the identity, nationality/registration jurisdiction, date of birth/incorporation, ID/unified number, contribution type and amount of every director, supervisor, manager and any shareholder holding ≥10% of issued shares or paid-in capital; every transfer that moves a holder above or below the 10% threshold, or any officer change, must be declared to the same platform within 15 days of the event. The annual confirmation must reconcile share-transfer records with the Register of Members and the foreign-investment permit held from MOEAIC so that the declared beneficial ownership matches the SIFN-approved investment structure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (股東名簿) — kept at the registered office, updated with each share transfer
Register of Directors and Supervisors (董事及監察人名冊) — with names, IDs and residential addresses
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Meetings (股東會議事錄及董事會議事錄)
Register of Share Pledges and Corporate Bonds (股權質押及公司債券存根簿) — if applicable

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (profit-seeking enterprise income tax, Income Tax Act Art. 5(5))
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: First NT$120,000 of annual taxable income exempt for qualifying enterprises; R&D and smart-machinery/5G investment tax credits under the Statute for Industrial Innovation (Art. 10 and Art. 10-1) creditable up to 30% of annual tax payable; 12% AMT on overly tax-exempt income; an additional 5% surtax levied on undistributed retained earnings (Art. 66-9) creates an effective 24.6% combined burden on profits not distributed.
